reference.title: Escalation Matrix for Security Cases
reference.shortdesc: Who the analyst on shift tells, how quickly, and through which channel, for each severity of case at Norrbyn Utilities. The matrix applies to every case the SOC opens, whatever raised it. Fictional sample written for this portfolio: the roles are real kinds of roles, and the people behind them aren’t named.

strow.stentry: An attempt that failed, from outside, against something that isn’t exposed. No sign of success, no internal source.
A port scan. A brute-force attempt against users that don’t exist.
An attempt with a chance of success, or anything from an internal source until it’s explained.
A brute-force attempt against accounts that exist. Malware blocked on a workstation. An internal host probing another.
Evidence that an attacker got in, or that data left.
A successful sign-in from an attacking source. Ransomware activity. Credentials found in a public place.
High, and the safety of people or the supply of water or power is affected or threatened.
Access to a control-system network. A compromised engineering workstation that can reach field devices.

section.title: Who to Tell, and When
section.p: The clock starts at the finding that set the severity, not at the alert.

strow.stentry: Nobody now. Summarise in the shift handover.
The SOC lead, in the daily review. If found at night, the SOC lead by message.
Next daily review, or one hour at night
Case comment with the Review tag; the SOC channel at night
Phone call from the on-call rota, then the case number by message
The incident lead on call, then the operations duty manager.
Phone calls. Don’t rely on messages at this severity.

section.p: If the incident lead doesn’t answer within ten minutes, call the next person on the rota. Record every call you make in the case, answered or not.

section.title: What to Have Ready When You Call

ol.li: The severity and the finding that set it, in one sentence.
What you have already done, including any block.
What you want decided, such as isolating a host, locking an account, or calling someone else in.

strow.stentry: Block an external address for 24 hours
Inform the regulator or the police
The head of security, with legal counsel
Communications, on the head of security’s request

section.title: Handover
section.p: A High or Critical case never changes hands without a conversation. At the end of a shift, the analyst walks the next analyst through the case timeline, and both add a handover comment. The incident lead stays the same until they hand over themselves.
